As for transgender vs transtrender, I guess I have two main points. I'm giving you the TL;DR version here, but transgendered individuals feel very strongly and intuitively that they ought to be the sex (a person's "sex," in medicine, refers to someone's chromosomal makeup) that they are not. The discrepancy between their intuitions and the reality of their bodies is an extremely disconcerting and distressing experience, and the best that medicine currently seems to be able to offer is hormone therapy and cosmetic surgery to attempt to fix the discrepancy. There are numerous brain imaging studies that support the idea that transgendered individuals are somehow neurologically different, but whether or not they are, I really just don't care whether someone wants to physically alter their bodies or take hormones. But a key difference is that transgendered people will typically try very hard to present themselves as members of the sex they feel they ought to be (male or female).

Transtrenders are simply people who want to change their pronouns, or even make up their own, individual pronoun to go by because they don't feel like the pronoun that typically corresponds to their sex "describes them," or something. They don't undergo any medical procedures, they just insist on being called a particular pronoun that they think describes them. My problem with that is that it completely misses the point of pronouns. Pronouns do not describe. They are a tool to allow for the easy flow of language so that you don't have to keep repeating the same noun over and over again. That's it. At most, pronouns can be said to describe what your genitals might be like. Anyone who wants a word that describes them in any more detail already has one: Their name. Having a pronoun that is unique to you is functionally identical to having a second name. Calling yourself "trans" because you want a second name is silly, pointless, and conflates you with a population that has a medically recognized condition.
